clues: A river name derived from an Indigenous expression for great water suits this landscape’s scale.
Subtropical forest around the water supports animals such as tapirs, howler monkeys and jaguars.
Many cascades drop across a basaltic escarpment, filling the air with spray.
The waterfall system forms part of the border between Argentina and Brazil.
Find the Argentine national park beside the immense horseshoe-shaped waterfall complex shared with Brazil.
targetLabel: Iguazú National Park — designated property reference point
modernContext: UNESCO’s published representative point for the designated property, not its uniquely correct centre.
explanation: The answer is the Argentine protected property associated with the shared waterfall system. Its Indigenous etymology is attributed to UNESCO’s account rather than used to imply a single universal spelling. The official reference point represents the park; the cascades and the neighbouring Brazilian park occupy a much larger area.
dateLabel: First UNESCO World Heritage inscription year, not the age of the natural feature
cultures: Physical geography, conservation and scientific study
uncertainty: Source-checked authoring only; independent factual, English and clue-order review is pending. The point represents the designated property, not every part of a large natural feature. Source descriptions and dynamic environmental conditions may differ in date or extent; precise current measurements are not implied.
